hints: Think about what Le Chatelier's principle says when you raise temperature or lower pressure, and which side of the equilibrium is favoured each time.
Higher temperature favouring products tells you the forward reaction must absorb heat, so look for a positive $\Delta H$ value.
Lower pressure favouring products tells you there must be more moles of gas on the product side, so count gas moles on each side to finish the match.
walkthrough:
**Use temperature to find the sign of ΔH**

Think of heat as a reactant or product. If raising temperature gives more product, the equilibrium shifts forward to absorb the extra heat.

That means the forward reaction is endothermic:
$$\Delta H > 0$$

**Use pressure to compare moles of gas**

Lowering pressure favours the side with more gas molecules, because the system tries to raise pressure again by making more particles.

So we need:
$$\text{moles of gas (products)} > \text{moles of gas (reactants)}$$

**Test each equation against both conditions**

Only one equation has both $\Delta H = +206 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (endothermic forward) and 2 moles of gas going to 4 moles of gas.

That equation satisfies increased temperature and decreased pressure both increasing product yield.

options.A: Forward reaction is endothermic with $\Delta H = +206 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, so higher temperature shifts equilibrium to the right. Reactants have 2 gas moles ($\text{CH}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$) and products have 4 gas moles ($3\text{H}_2 + \text{CO}$), so lower pressure also shifts equilibrium to the right. Both conditions match.
options.B: This is exothermic in the forward direction ($\Delta H$ negative), so increasing temperature would shift equilibrium left and decrease product yield. Students who only count gas moles (7 to 8) may pick this for the pressure effect but forget to check the temperature condition.
options.C: This is exothermic ($\Delta H$ negative) and goes from 2 gas moles to 1 gas mole. Increasing temperature favours reactants, and decreasing pressure also favours reactants (the side with more moles). It is the exact opposite of what is required.
options.D: This is endothermic ($\Delta H$ positive) so high temperature does favour products, but it goes from 3 gas moles to 2 gas moles. Decreasing pressure would therefore favour reactants and lower the yield. This traps students who check only temperature.
